exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $80,509.00 as of 2026-11-05 05:39:50 UTC, -0.04% over one hour and +3.78% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $77,670.00 to $81,004.00; spot sits at 85% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is +0.89% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($79,516.75) is above the 72-hour average ($78,011.95). Spot is 1.45% below the seven-day high of $81,691.75 and 5.66% above the seven-day low of $76,198.52.

exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 2.00% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 70.7, conventionally overbought.

exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $35.87 billion, equal to 2.22% of the $1.62 trillion market capitalization.

exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 50 ("Neutral"), versus 51 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink BTC/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $80,600.37, 53 minutes before the spot quote and +0.11% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is firmly anchored near the upper 85 % of its 24‑hour range ([Ex. B]) and has posted a 3.78 % gain in the last day ([Ex. A]), indicating that bullish pressure is sustaining the current level rather than a fleeting spike.  

2. Momentum metrics corroborate this strength: realized volatility is modest at 2.00 % per day ([Ex. D]), while the 14‑hour RSI sits at 70.7, a classic over‑bought signal that often precedes continued upward thrust in a low‑volatility environment.  

3. Market infrastructure supports a long stance: liquidity remains ample with $35.87 billion traded in 24 hours ([Ex. E]), and the Chainlink oracle—our settlement reference—quotes $80,600.37, a 0.11 % premium to the spot ([Ex. G]), confirming that execution will occur at a favorable price.  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is effectively flat on the hour (-0.04%) and has risen 3.78% in 24 hours, placing it at the 85th percentile of the day’s range [Ex. A, B]; this indicates a firm near‑term support level that can sustain a short‑term dip without breaking lower‑side liquidity.  

2. Despite a modest 0.89% weekly gain, the market shows overbought momentum (RSI 70.7) and a neutral fear‑greed reading (50) that historically precede corrective pull‑backs [Ex. C, D, F]; the overbought condition suggests price pressure will reverse within the next trading day.  

3. Liquidity remains ample ($35.87 bn, 2.22% of market cap) and the Chainlink feed, the settlement benchmark, sits $91 above spot, confirming a reliable pricing reference for a short practice position [Ex. E, G]; this mitigates execution risk for the Bear.  

For these reasons the Bear respectfully moves to open a short practice position. The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s claim of “firm near‑term support” is speculative; the price sits only 1.45 % below its seven‑day high and 5.66 % above its seven‑day low, indicating ample headroom for a breakout rather than a cushion [Ex. C]. Moreover, the “overbought RSI” does not guarantee a reversal—RSI 70.7 can persist in a strong bull trend, and the market’s neutral Fear & Greed index (50) signals no imminent panic, undermining the Bear’s corrective narrative [Ex. D, F]. Consequently, the evidence does not substantiate a short‑term dip sufficient to justify a short practice position. Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s first point hinges on the 85 % range placement, yet Exhibit B shows the price is still 15 % below the 24‑hour high, leaving ample headroom for reversal; the modest 3.78 % gain in Exhibit A is merely a recovery from a prior dip, not a sustained rally.  

Second, the Bull glorifies the 14‑hour RSI of 70.7 as bullish, but Exhibit D defines any RSI above 70 as overbought, a classic precursor to pull‑back, especially when paired with the low 2.00 % realized volatility that limits upside momentum.  

Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds the evidence insufficient to justify a practice position.

findings.finding: Spot price up 3.78% in 24h but flat hour‑to‑hour, showing limited momentum
RSI 70.7 indicates overbought condition while realized volatility is low at 2.00% per day
Fear & Greed Index at 50 denotes neutral sentiment, offering no clear directional bias

ruling.opinion: The price’s modest 24‑hour gain and position near the 85% range point to short‑term strength, yet the overbought RSI and neutral sentiment signal potential correction, while low volatility limits upside thrust. These opposing forces leave the net outlook ambiguous, preventing a confident long or short stance. Consequently, the Court cannot endorse a practice position for the next 24 hours.
ruling.dissent: The Bear argues that overbought RSI and neutral sentiment strongly favor a corrective pull‑back, justifying a short position.

sentence.reason: The case was dismissed; no practice position is ordered.
